title: 27-Inch 4K vs QHD Monitor for Productivity: Which Makes Sense?
summary: At 27 inches, QHD is usually the balanced productivity choice when you want more workspace without heavy scaling or a demanding graphics connection. 4K gives finer detail and more pixels, but may require operating-system scaling and a capable computer. Choose by text comfort, apps, viewing distance and workflow—not by pixel count alone.

title: Monitor Distance and Desk Depth: Set Up a Comfortable Viewing Position
summary: There is no single perfect monitor distance for everyone. OSHA gives a general preferred range of about 20–40 inches, while stressing readable text and neutral posture. Start by centering the monitor, sitting back with support, and adjusting text size so you do not lean forward. Desk depth should accommodate that comfortable position plus keyboard space.

title: USB-C Monitor vs Dock: Build a One-Cable Laptop Setup Without Guesswork
summary: A USB-C monitor can replace a separate dock when it supports the video mode, charging wattage and downstream ports your laptop needs. A dock is more flexible for several displays and peripherals. USB-C describes a connector, not a guaranteed feature set, so verify the exact laptop, monitor, cable and dock capabilities as a complete chain.

title: Monitor with Built-In KVM vs Separate KVM Switch: Which Fits Two Computers?

title: IPS vs VA vs OLED for Office Monitors: Match the Panel to Your Room
summary: For general office work, a good IPS monitor is a dependable all-rounder; VA can suit users who value contrast, while OLED delivers deep blacks and fast pixel response at a higher price and with different long-term-use considerations. Exact models matter more than panel labels. Compare measured performance, text appearance, room lighting, warranty and your workload.

title: Monitor Light Bar vs Desk Lamp: Reduce Glare and Light the Work Area
summary: A monitor light bar is a space-saving way to light the desk without a lamp base, while a desk lamp offers wider placement and can illuminate paper or objects more flexibly. Neither guarantees glare-free viewing. Choose a light source you can aim away from the screen, control for brightness and color, and position alongside the window and monitor.

title: Matte vs Glossy Monitor in a Bright Room: Manage Reflections First
